_why: Mutant ids declared BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING for UpdateZeroMQ, each with the reason. `vit_mutate.py --equivalences` reads the KEYS of this object, so the reasons live in the same file as the claim, and a declared mutant leaves the denominator -- every entry is a claim that has to be answerable. EIGHT are declared, more than any other unit in this campaign, and they fall into TWO reasons rather than eight. Seven of them are UNOBSERVABLE rather than equivalent-by-the-standard, and all seven are unobservable for one reason stated once in harness/ranges.toml: this unit's eight `LocalVar%ZMQ_*` outputs are copied out of `setpoints(8)`, which NOTHING WRITES in the configuration this campaign compiles, so the reference has no answer on them and they are excluded from the comparison. A mutant that can only move an output no oracle covers cannot be killed by any corpus, and saying so is not the same as saying it is harmless. What was NOT declared is the larger number: the first scoring run left FORTY survivors at 0.2593 (mutation/UpdateZeroMQ.survivors_before_restatements.json), and thirty-two of those are gone -- not declared -- because the corpus was widened (harness/generate.py R9) and two restatements were removed from the translation with the proof written into it. A survivor is a question about the instrument until the instrument has been asked.
ac7a5b72: compare_op '>' -> '>=' at `if (static_cast<int32_t>(s.size()) > ErrVar->n_ErrMsg_cap)` in `assign_errmsg`, updatezeromq.cpp. The two forms differ on exactly one input, `s.size() == n_ErrMsg_cap`. `s.size()` is one of two compile-time strings here -- the 105-character ZeroMQ message, and the same message behind `UpdateZeroMQ:` -- and `n_ErrMsg_cap` is `LEN(ErrMsg) + 4096` in the differential harness (harness/emit.py ALLOC_HEADROOM) and `LEN(src%ErrMsg) + VIT_DEFERRED_CHAR_HEADROOM`, the same 4096, in the integrated build (vit_errorvariables_view.f90:63). The capacity is therefore at least 4096 in every configuration this campaign can build, the guard is true in all of them, and no case at any length or flag value can separate `>` from `>=`. SAME SITE, SAME REASON, SAME DECLARATION as ReadAvrSWAP's e82a5f90 and ExtController's 11d2c9cc -- the third unit to reach the `CHARACTER(:), ALLOCATABLE` assignment idiom, and the reason has not changed. NOT REMOVED: the guard is what makes an over-long assignment a REFUSAL rather than a truncation, and a truncated error message is the one wrong answer a bit comparison cannot catch. Note the asymmetry with the OTHER `>` on this file's live path -- `CntrPar%ZMQ_Mode > 0` against `>= 0` -- which the widened corpus KILLS on 7 of 8334 cases, the cases where ZMQ_Mode is exactly 0 AND the rate gate is satisfied in the same case. Both were survivors before R9; only this one still is.
262bd4b6: const_tweak '0.0' -> '1.0' at `const double no_setpoint = 0.0;`. This is the value the reference copies out of its unwritten `setpoints` array, and it reaches ONLY the eight `LocalVar%ZMQ_*` fields, all six of which are declared no-oracle in harness/ranges.toml. Measured, not assumed: evidence/UpdateZeroMQ/setpoints_indeterminate.run.txt shows the reference answering `NaN`, then `1.0`, then `-7.25` on three calls in one process, tracking whatever the previous stack frame left. A mutant that writes 1.0 where the translation writes 0.0 is a different arbitrary choice of a value the reference does not define. UNOBSERVABLE, not equivalent: the quantity is real, and no comparison against this reference can constrain it.
059e4ae8: index_offset '[0]' -> '[0 + 1]' at `LocalVar->ZMQ_PitOffset[0] = no_setpoint;`. Writes `ZMQ_PitOffset(2)` instead of `ZMQ_PitOffset(1)`; both are inside the same no-oracle field, and both receive the same value, so even the field's own bytes are unchanged -- the only difference is that `ZMQ_PitOffset(1)` keeps its incoming value, which is what the reference leaves indeterminate anyway. Same reason as 262bd4b6.
c14786fd: index_offset '[1]' -> '[1 + 1]' at `LocalVar->ZMQ_PitOffset[1] = no_setpoint;`. Same reason as 059e4ae8.
05a7518b: index_offset '[2]' -> '[2 + 1]' at `LocalVar->ZMQ_PitOffset[2] = no_setpoint;`. Same reason as 059e4ae8, with one difference stated rather than smoothed over: `ZMQ_PitOffset[3]` is PAST THE END of a `double ZMQ_PitOffset[3]` member, so this mutant is undefined behaviour and not merely unobservable. What it writes is decided by the struct's layout: `localvariables_view_t` declares `double ZMQ_PitOffset[3]; double ZMQ_R_Speed;` adjacently, so the write lands in `ZMQ_R_Speed` -- which is itself no-oracle, and receives the same 0.0. Declared on the same footing as the other seven and flagged here because an out-of-bounds survivor is the shape unit #15 recorded: it cannot be killed by a value comparison and it must not be called harmless without saying which bytes it touches.
4d9354a7: const_tweak '0' -> '1' -- the subscript literal of `LocalVar->ZMQ_PitOffset[0]` read as a constant rather than as an index. The same mutation as 059e4ae8 reached by a second operator, and the same reason.
f7d2b75f: const_tweak '1' -> '2' -- the subscript literal of `LocalVar->ZMQ_PitOffset[1]`. Same reason as c14786fd.
5d6e6e0c: const_tweak '2' -> '3' -- the subscript literal of `LocalVar->ZMQ_PitOffset[2]`. Same reason as 05a7518b, including the out-of-bounds note.
